explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/87: for ε > 0, is R(G) > (1−ε)^k R(k) for every G with χ(G) = k, once k is large? The statement adds ε < 1. That loses nothing: the claim for small ε implies it for larger ε < 1, and for ε ∈ [1,2) the claim is trivial. For ε > 2 the literal reading gives (ε−1)^k for even k, an artefact of the informal statement. G ranges over finite simple graphs with chromaticNumber = k, R(G) is diagonalGraphRamsey (the least n such that every graph on Fin n contains G or its complement does) and R(k) = R(K_k, K_k). Faithful.
